newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shares close higher on Nasdaq gains.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shares close higher on Nasdaq gains.

text.p: Tel Aviv stocks closed higher on Thursday in rising turnover following the gains posted by Israeli shares traded in the United States, traders said.
The benchmark Mishtanim index of the top 100 shares rose 1.56 percent, or 2.96 points. to 192.33 on all share turnover of 80 million shekels against 61 million on Wednesday.
The Maof 25 blue chip index gained 1.42 percent to 202.16.

"The rise of Israeli shares traded on Nasdaq was the main reason for today's rise. The Israeli market was also up following other financial markets which rose after the re-election of U.S. President Bill Clinton," said Eli Nahum, head of trading at Zannex Securities.
"The mood in the market has improved and turnover is rising but it is still too early to talk about a positive change," Nahum added.

"Activity has improved after two weeks when turnover averaged around 40 million shekels. The market was reacting to the rise of Israeli shares on Nasdaq and the positive mood in the other stock markets abroad," said Yoram Ben Yaeir at Ahrayut Investment Management.

Teva Pharmaceutical Industries, the most active share, surged 4.5 percent to 144,891 on volume of 10.6 million shekels, after its American depositary receipts traded on Nasdaq gained 5.5 percent on Wednesday.

Tadiran Ltd rose 3.0 percent to 1,465 after its shares in New York gained 2.3 percent on Wednesday. Tadiran rose in New York after its subsidiary Tadiran Telecommunications posted third-quarter earnings per share of $0.36 against $0.21 a year earlier.

Bezeq Israel Telecom, the only loser on the Maof, fell 2.25 percent to 807. On Wednesday Israel opened international phone calling to competition for the first time. Two multinational consortia were awarded licences to compete with state-controlled Bezeq.
Industrial Buildings rose 1.5 percent to 291 despite announcing that net profit in the third quarter fell to 11 million shekels from 14.4 million shekels.
Nice Systems surged 5.0 percent to 6,881 after it posted third-quarter earnings per share of $0.22 against a loss of $0.03 a year earlier.
Discount Investments Corp rose 2.5 percent to 19,096 after UBS Securities rated it a "buy". Discount's parent companies IDB Holding Corp and IDB Development were rated "hold".
IDB Holding rose 1.75 percent to 1,129 while IDB Development gained 2.0 percent to 5,127.

Other active shares include Bank Hapoalim, which gained 1.0 percent to 457 on volume of 5.7 million shekels; and Koor Industries, the parent of Tadiran, which rose 1.5 percent to 28,461 on turnover of 5.6 million shekels.
